title: fix(spec): a TEXT column is exactly compatible with `signature` / `qrcode` fields
body:
Fixes #12117

`CANONICAL_TO_FIELD`'s `text` row in `packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts` gains `signature` and `qrcode` in its `exact` set. The `binary` row is unchanged — that half was a measurement, and the measurement said leave it (below).

## Why

After #11875 (maintainer ruling 2026-08-25), an unbounded TEXT column is the platform's **own emitted physical shape** for `signature` / `qrcode`: `sql-driver.ts` emits both in its text family alongside `richtext` / `code` (`sql-driver.ts:14015` and `:14371`, both returning the text-family answer), and their stored value is a string — routinely a data-URI — per `STRING_VALUE_TYPES` and `valueSchemaFor`, which returns `z.string()` for both.

The compat table had not followed. Consequence on `main`: `IExternalDatasourceService.validateObject` introspecting a table **the driver itself created** diffed a `text` column holding a signature against the `signature` field that wrote it and reported `type_mismatch`; `generateObjectDraft` would not offer either type for a TEXT column. This is consistency restoration with the ruled route, not a new decision — the triage comment on #12117 says so in as many words.

## The `binary.exact` half — measured, not guessed

Triage asked whether `signature` should leave `binary.exact`, to be decided from a reading rather than a guess. It stays. Three measurements, all re-runnable:

**1. No binary-payload signature path exists.** Population: 5182 tracked `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.mts`/`.mjs`/`.js` files. 20 of them mention the `signature` / `qrcode` field type as a quoted literal; 3 of those also carry binary-payload vocabulary (`Buffer` / `Uint8Array` / `ArrayBuffer` / `bytea` / `varbinary` / `BLOB` / `binary`). All three are controlled:

| File | Co-occurrence | Control |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` | `t.binary()` at `:10735` | Inside the **remote-column introspection** mapping (`ty.includes('blob') \|\| ty.includes('binary')`) — a foreign column's type, never a field-type → column mapping. The driver's own `signature` cases return the TEXT-family answer. |
| `packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts` | `'signature'` at `:785`, `:819` | A presigned-token *cryptographic* signature, not the field type. |
| `packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.ts` | — | The table under review. |

So nothing in the monorepo stores a `signature` field value as bytes, and the `binary` entry is not load-bearing for any platform write.

**2. The entry is import-side reach, and dropping it would single `signature` out with no evidence asking for it.** This row is not a stored-value-shape claim: `file` and `image` are `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES`, whose stored value is a reference-id **string**, so no member of `binary.exact` round-trips as bytes. What the row says is that a remote BLOB column can carry this class of *content* — which a foreign schema (the only kind this matrix is ever asked about) may well do for a captured signature image, exactly as it may for an image.

**3. Membership is many-to-many by design, so nothing was displaced.** Measured on `origin/main` before the edit: 9 field types are already exact under more than one canonical column — `text` under `text` / `uuid` / `enum`; `select` under `text` / `enum`; `tags` and `multiselect` under `json` / `array`; `number` under four numeric rows. `isCompatible` is keyed on the *column*, so the two memberships answer questions about two different columns and can never collide.

No dual-storage story turned up, so there is no open question here — the reading is decisive and is now recorded in the file, which was #12117's stated purpose ("recording the drift so the next reader of `type-compat.ts` is told").

## Tests

`packages/spec/src/data/type-compat.test.ts` gains two cases: one pinning that a TEXT column serves every string-valued type in the `text` row (the whole row, so the next type to join the driver's text family has to be added deliberately rather than drift out again), across the dialect spellings the column arrives under from introspection (`varchar(255)`, `clob`, postgres `citext`, bigquery `STRING`); one pinning the many-to-many property itself, `signature` exact under both `text` and `bytea`, alongside the pre-existing `text` / `uuid` / `enum` precedent.

**Reverse-verification** (fix committed first, so the restore leg has a recovery point). Predicted direction: **turns red**. Mutation: revert the two types out of the `text` row. Proven on disk before measuring — worktree blob `5d8c699f` → `6fcf721a`, and the anchored text flipped (`grep -c` of the removed text 1 → 0, of the injected text 0 → 1). Observed: `2 failed | 13 passed`, both failures being the new cases, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. Restore leg proven the same way: `git checkout HEAD -- <abs path>` (never bare — that reads the index), then `git diff HEAD` empty and the blob back to `5d8c699f` byte-identically. The script carried a `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, but the hash comparison is the proof, not the trap firing.

No rebuild was needed for either leg: the test imports `./type-compat` by relative path within its own package, so no `dist/` sits between the mutation and the assertion.

## Gates

All run under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, on the final commit **`c1d4445`**, tree clean. The family list was re-derived from the actual change set with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (3 paths vs merge base `2e2411571`), not from the dispatch prompt's list.

Green (each quoting its own verdict line, exit captured before any pipe): `check:nul-bytes` · `check:changeset-gate-self-tests` · `check:cross-package-test-inputs` ("OK: 18 package(s) read outside themselves, all declared") · `check:merge-driver` · `check:objectui-changeset` · `check:page-declaration-shape` · `check:published-files` · `check:slot-lookup` · `check:spec-parsed-alias` · `check:test-source-alias` · `check:type-source-resolution` · `check:query-options-erasure` · `check:engine-double-contract` · `check:where-matcher` · `check:type-check-coverage` · `check-adr-0087-registration` · `check-changeset-no-major` · `check-ci-filter-parity` · `check-comment-mask-adoption` · `check-dev-prereqs` · `check-empty-changeset` · `check-plugin-teardown-shape` · `docs-audit/check-affected-docs` · `docs-audit/check-drift-comment` · `release-rehearsal-clone --self-test` · spec's `check:empty-state` / `check:liveness` / `check:strictness-ledger` / `check:variant-docs` · `@objectstack/lint check:doc-formula-expressions`.

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` (type-compat + field-value): `Test Files 2 passed (2) · Tests 36 passed (36)`. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: green, and **confirmed to have read the edited files** rather than merely reporting green over them — `tsc --listFiles` puts `type-compat.ts` in the main program and *both* `type-compat.ts` and `type-compat.test.ts` in `tsconfig.test.json`'s program.

`check-dev-prereqs`, `@objectstack/lint check:doc-formula-expressions` and `check:type-check-debt` first returned `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` on the unbuilt worktree — NOT MEASURED, not red. The full closure was built (`turbo run build --concurrency=2 --filter=./packages/* --filter=./packages/*/*`, 70/70 successful) and all three re-run green; `check:type-check-debt --re-measure` reports "32 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 273.0s, 1843 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number."

Repo-wide `pnpm lint` was left to CI, which runs the farm exactly once regardless — declared narrowing, not a silent skip.

## Changeset

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, following what the comparable type-compat/text-family PRs did (`.changeset/richtext-code-text-family-emission.md`, `.changeset/signature-qrcode-bounded-text-family.md`) — this changes `isCompatible`'s exported behaviour, so it is user-visible and not a `skip-changeset` case.

## Not regenerated

Nothing derives a doc projection from `CANONICAL_TO_FIELD`. `content/docs/references/data/external-catalog.mdx` is generated from `external-catalog.zod.ts` and mentions the matrix only in two field descriptions; ADR-0015 §4.6 describes the module in prose and carries no copy of the table.
